```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(snpflowR)
```

## Scope

This development package computes exploratory summaries of biallelic allele
frequencies. It does not identify migration uniquely. Two populations can have
the same observed frequencies under different histories of drift, founding,
selection, and migration. Bootstrap stability cannot resolve this identifiability
problem. A supported genetic contrast therefore is not a supported causal history.

The current implementation is restricted to diploid hard calls or integer allele
counts with aligned alleles. A pooled read count is not a chromosome count.
Before analysis, establish the sampling design, quality filters, population
labels, neutral-locus assumptions, and an appropriate linkage treatment.

## Estimator and orientation

For an eligible locus, let p and q be alternate-allele frequencies in A and B.
The hypothetical pool has alternate frequency

$$r = \frac{\sqrt{pq}}{\sqrt{pq} + \sqrt{(1-p)(1-q)}}.$$

The pool construction is from Sundqvist et al. (2016), DOI
[10.1002/ece3.2096](https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.2096). For A versus the pool,
the total heterozygosity and between-sample component simplify to

$$H_{T,A} = (p+r)\{1-(p+r)/2\}, \qquad D_A = (p-r)^2/2.$$

Across the same set of usable loci in both directions, the package computes

$$G_{A\to B} = \frac{\sum_l D_{A,l}}{\sum_l H_{T,A,l}},
\qquad \Delta_{AB} = G_{B\to A} - G_{A\to B}.$$

This is a ratio of sums, not an average of per-SNP ratios. The two populations
have equal weight in each diversity comparison; their observed chromosome
counts determine frequencies and eligibility. This plug-in GST is not a
finite-sample corrected FST estimator. Positive delta indicates greater
similarity of A to the pool, giving an A-to-B signal under the model.

The descriptive transform `(1 / GST - 1) / 4` reverses the ordering. We expose
it without treating it as absolute migration. The normalized matrix divides
finite values by the largest value in the analyzed set, provided no value is
infinite. Adding populations can change that scale. The contrast and its
interval are computed before normalization.

## Degenerate loci and pairs

| Situation | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Too few called allele copies in either population | Exclude from both directions; count `n_low_calls` |
| Both populations fixed for the same allele | No information; count `n_shared_fixed` |
| Populations fixed for opposite alleles | Pool undefined; exclude both directions; count `n_no_shared` |
| No directional denominator | Return NA and an unresolved reason |
| Identical polymorphic populations | GST zero; transformed value infinite; direction unresolved |
| Too few contributing loci/blocks or bootstrap draws | Report estimates, label direction unresolved |

The opposite-fixation exclusion is a deliberate extension choice, different
from the original paper's proposed maximum-differentiation convention.
Symmetric pairwise GST retains these loci. Consequently, directional and
symmetric estimates can summarize different sets; audit the exclusion columns.
No equivalence with another package is claimed for these edge cases.

## Genotype and count inputs

```{r inputs}
g <- rbind(c(0, 1, NA), c(1, 2, 0), c(2, 1, 1), c(1, 0, 2))
colnames(g) <- c("snp1", "snp2", "snp3")
x <- genotype_counts(g, c("A", "A", "B", "B"))
x$alt
x$called
```

Missing genotypes contribute zero called allele copies. No imputation occurs.
For a count matrix, supply `snp_counts(alt, called)` with populations in rows,
loci in columns, and exactly matching names. The alternate allele must refer
to the same allele in both populations for every column.

```{r vcf}
file <- system.file("extdata", "tiny.vcf", package = "snpflowR")
vcf_counts <- read_snp_vcf(file, c(a1 = "A", a2 = "A", b1 = "B", b2 = "B"),
                           block_size = 100000)
vcf_counts$import
```

VCF sample labels align by ID. Phasing is discarded after allele counting.
Partial missing calls such as `0/.` are treated as missing entire diploid
genotypes. Unsupported ploidy errors; unsupported variant types are counted
and skipped. The fixture has too little information for inference. The reader
does not evaluate per-genotype DP, GQ, PL, or FT, and retains count matrices in
memory. Filter poor-quality calls before import.

## QC and paired resampling

The default QC filter does not impose a positive minor-allele frequency cutoff:
rare and private alleles affect this estimator. If a cutoff is justified, report
it and examine sensitivity. Pooled MAF weights observed chromosomes, so unequal
sample sizes influence filtering.

```{r qc}
sim <- simulate_snp_flow(n_loci = 300, seed = 42)
filtered <- filter_snps(sim$counts, min_called = 10, min_maf = 0)
head(filtered$qc)
```

Locus resampling requires an explicit independence assumption. For linked
data, supply block labels to `snp_counts()` or physical windows to the VCF
reader. Sample entire blocks with replacement and keep both population
directions paired. Variable-length blocks retain their original sizes and can
produce different SNP totals per replicate. Blocks must approximate independent
sampling units; the software cannot establish this from labels.

```{r estimate}
fit <- estimate_flow(filtered, n_boot = 999, resample = "locus", seed = 43)
fit$pairs
```

Intervals are percentile intervals for delta, using quantile type 7. Default
Bonferroni tail allocation counts every unordered population pair. It provides
a nominal multiplicity adjustment, not demonstrated family-wise error control
for biological migration. With many pairs, increase replicates until at least
five expected finite draws fall in each adjusted tail; otherwise the reporting
rule returns `insufficient_tail_resolution`.

The bootstrap conditions on the sampled individuals, input loci, and QC.
It does not propagate uncertainty about individual recruitment, genotype calls,
or filter selection. Resampling counts as though they were independent alleles
would impose additional assumptions and is not done here.

```{r plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3.2}
plot(fit)
```

## Reproducibility and interpretation

A supplied seed is local to the function and preserves the caller's random
stream. Results retain software versions, RNG kind, resampling settings, and
QC history. Preserve input checksums, the full result with `saveRDS()`, the
population map, and `sessionInfo()` in your own analysis records.

The initial development pilot shows that sampling imbalance and unequal
effective sizes can induce supported contrasts without migration. Founder
history can do the same. This finding prevents a claim that the package
reliably establishes contemporary gene-flow direction. See the repository's
validation records and research plan for the exact simulated scenarios and
remaining work. The built-in simulator is deliberately simple; independent
coalescent experiments and external review are needed in addition to unit tests.
